Response3868Ab39519D_BookSide.description: Side of the book for an order or trade. For event markets, this refers to the YES leg only: `bid` means buy YES, `ask` means sell YES. (Selling YES is economically equivalent to buying NO at `1 - price`, but this endpoint quotes everything from the YES side.)

Response3868Ab39519D_FixedPointCount.description: Fixed-point contract count string (2 decimals, e.g., "10.00"; referred to as "fp" in field names). Requests accept 0-2 decimal places (e.g., "10", "10.0", "10.00"); responses always emit 2 decimals. Fractional contract values (e.g., "2.50") are supported; the minimum granularity is 0.01 contracts.

Response3868Ab39519D_FixedPointDollars.description: Fixed-point US dollar string. Most request fields accept 2-4 decimal places (e.g., "0.56", "0.5600"); responses emit up to 6. Valid quote intervals for a given market are constrained by that market's price level structure.

cap_strike.description: Maximum expiration value that leads to a YES settlement

custom_strike.description: Expiration value for each target that leads to a YES settlement

early_close_condition.description: The condition under which the market can close early

expected_expiration_time.description: Time when this market is expected to expire

expiration_value.description: The value that was considered for the settlement

fee_waiver_expiration_time.description: Time when this market's fee waiver expires

floor_strike.description: Minimum expiration value that leads to a YES settlement

functional_strike.description: Mapping from expiration values to settlement values

is_provisional.description: If true, the market may be removed after determination if there is no activity on it

latest_expiration_time.description: Latest possible time for this market to expire

mve_collection_ticker.description: The ticker of the multivariate event collection

no_sub_title.description: Shortened title for the no side of this market

occurrence_datetime.description: The recorded datetime when the underlying event occurred, if available

price_level_structure.description: Price level structure for this market, defining price ranges and tick sizes

price_ranges.description: Valid price ranges for orders on this market

rules_primary.description: A plain language description of the most important market terms

rules_secondary.description: A plain language description of secondary market terms

settlement_bounds_type.description: Which settlement bounds apply to this market. default means the market has no settlement bounds

settlement_timer_seconds.description: The amount of time after determination that the market settles

settlement_ts.description: Timestamp when the market was settled. Only filled for settled markets

status.description: The current status of the market in its lifecycle.

strike_type.description: Strike type defines how the market strike is defined and evaluated

updated_time.description: Time of the last non-trading metadata update.

yes_sub_title.description: Shortened title for the yes side of this market

event_ticker.description: Unique identifier for the selected event

market_ticker.description: Unique identifier for the selected market

side.description: The side of the selected market

Response3868Ab39519D_OrderbookCountFp.description: Orderbook with fixed-point contract counts (fp) in all dollar price levels.

Response3868Ab39519D_PriceLevelDollarsCo.description: Price level in dollars represented as [dollars_string, fp] where dollars_string is like "0.1500" and fp is a FixedPointCount string (fixed-point contract count). The second element is the contract quantity (not price).

end.description: Ending price for this range in dollars

start.description: Starting price for this range in dollars

step.description: Price step/tick size for this range in dollars

created_time.description: Timestamp when this trade was executed

is_block_trade.description: True if this trade was matched off-book as a block trade (e.g. via RFQ / negotiated block proposal); false for trades that filled on the standard order book.

taker_outcome_side.description:
The outcome side the taker is positioned for. buy-yes and sell-no produce 'yes'; buy-no and sell-yes produce 'no'.

`taker_outcome_side` describes directional exposure only; it does not change the trade's price. A trade at price `p` with `taker_outcome_side=no` is matched against the maker at the same price `p` with the opposite direction — both parties trade at the same price.

`taker_outcome_side` and `taker_book_side` will become the canonical way to determine trade direction. The legacy `taker_side` field will be deprecated in a future release — please migrate to these new fields.

taker_side.description: Deprecated. Use `taker_outcome_side` (or `taker_book_side`) instead. See [Order direction](/getting_started/order_direction). This field will not be removed before May 14, 2026.
